cases.visibleGeometry: Broad smooth central slope is flanked by irregular shallow drainage. A sharply bounded, roughly polygonal raised form lies at the lower right, with a fairly level top and steep edges. A faint diagonal track or break crosses the upper left.
cases.alternatives: The polygonal form could be a modern tank, stockpile, quarry remnant or engineered platform. Drainage and small bumps may be natural erosion or vegetation-related surface noise.
cases.supportLimits: Most of the form appears measured, with interpolated patches around its margins. Its sharp outline and flatness need source-return and present-day imagery checks.

candidates.nextCheck: Inspect original ground returns, cross-sections and recent imagery for a modern engineered object.

cases.visibleGeometry: Several narrow incisions converge near the centre and continue toward the lower edge. Low rounded terrain occupies both sides; the right side has irregular small bumps and short parallel marks. The strongest linear forms follow the drainage network.
cases.alternatives: Natural runoff erosion, tracks or field drainage could explain the lines; small bumps may reflect vegetation, stones or processing noise.
cases.supportLimits: The central incision has substantial interpolated ground, especially near the convergence. Its apparent edges and depth are unreliable without original returns.

cases.visibleGeometry: Dense, regularly spaced curved ridges cover the left field; finer nearly horizontal ridges cover the right. A strong north-south field edge separates them, and another straight edge crosses the lower right. A few isolated small rises lie in the right field.
cases.alternatives: Cultivation or terracing, field boundaries and agricultural disturbance explain the regular spacing and alignment. Isolated rises may be rocks, spoil or vegetation artifacts.
cases.supportLimits: Most field surfaces are measured. The north-south boundary and lower-right edge include interpolated cells, so small discontinuities there need source-return confirmation.

cases.visibleGeometry: Mostly smooth ground contains scattered small rounded rises. The most pronounced is near the upper left, with a narrow line extending south. A loose cluster of smaller bumps lies near the centre-right, and another pair near the lower centre. No continuous enclosure or broad platform is clear.
cases.alternatives: Rocks, shrubs or tree-root mounds, spoil and modern ground disturbance could produce these rises. The narrow line could be a path or survey/processing artifact.
cases.supportLimits: The bumps are mostly on measured model cells, but their sizes are small and individual return patterns are unverified. Image relief alone cannot establish whether they are constructed.

candidates.feature: Small isolated rise with adjacent linear mark
candidates.nextCheck: Inspect original ground returns and current aerial imagery for rock, vegetation or recent disturbance.
